INTERNAL INCIDENT REPORT - RANSOMWARE INTRUSION AT REGIONAL WATER UTILITY

Reference: IR-2024-0917
Classification: For Official Use Only
Prepared by: Computer Security Incident Response Team

Summary

On 12 September 2024 at approximately 02:40 local time, monitoring analysts at a
regional water utility observed anomalous outbound traffic from an engineering
workstation on the corporate network. Within ninety minutes the intrusion had
progressed to the deployment of file-encrypting malware across eleven servers,
including the utility's billing platform and its historian database. Operational
technology systems that control treatment and distribution were segmented from the
affected network and were not encrypted. Water quality and supply were not
affected at any point.

Initial Access

Forensic review indicates the attacker gained initial access through a reused
credential belonging to a third-party maintenance contractor. The credential had
not been rotated in fourteen months and was not protected by multi-factor
authentication. The attacker authenticated to an internet-facing remote access
portal on 4 September and maintained a low-profile foothold for eight days before
escalating.

Lateral Movement and Impact

The attacker used a common open-source post-exploitation framework to move from
the initial workstation to a domain controller, where they created two rogue
administrator accounts. Backups stored on a network share were deleted before
encryption began. Offline backups held at a separate site were intact and became
the basis for recovery. Billing operations were restored within four days;
full restoration of historian data took nine days.

Indicators of Compromise

- Command-and-control domain: update-svc-sync.net
- Attacker IP address: 185.220.101.47
- Dropped payload SHA-256: 9f2c4e1a7b6d8c3f5a0e2d4b6c8a1f3e5d7c9b0a2e4f6d8c0b2a4e6f8d0c2b4a6
- Ransom note filename: RESTORE-FILES-NOW.txt

Recommended Actions

Rotate all contractor credentials immediately and enforce multi-factor
authentication on every remote access path. Isolate backup infrastructure so that
domain administrator accounts cannot reach it. Deploy endpoint detection and
response agents to all servers and engineering workstations. Conduct a tabletop
exercise covering a scenario in which corporate and operational networks must be
decoupled under time pressure.

Outlook

There is no evidence that operational technology was targeted, but the intrusion
demonstrates that a corporate compromise can force protective shutdowns that
degrade service. The utility has requested assistance drafting external
communications for regulators and the public.
